overview: Holotype AM F66763 is a tooth-bearing dentary that anchors a specimen-level test of Mesozoic monotreme dental anatomy and affinity.

ecology.diet: Diet inferred from molar form; direct food evidence absent
ecology.habitat: Griman Creek depositional setting; habitual habitat unresolved
ecology.bodySize: Body size cannot be measured from the jaw alone
ecology.guild: Feeding guild unresolved beyond dental inference

traits: Dental characters compared with monotreme and tribosphenic conditions
evidenceSummary: The holotype directly records jaw and tooth morphology, while dental homology, affinity, diet and whole-body form remain interpretations and the specimen is not a direct ancestor.

overview: Articulated holotype CAGS 01-IG-1a,b preserves skull, dentition and postcranium used in competing therian matrices and a scansorial locomotor interpretation.

ecology.habitat: Yixian lacustrine ecosystem; habitual microhabitat inferred
ecology.locomotion: Scansoriality inferred from limb and foot proportions
ecology.bodySize: Small mammal represented by one articulated skeleton
ecology.guild: Small scansorial faunivore inferred from anatomy

traits: Character set with matrix-sensitive therian placement
evidenceSummary: The holotype supports anatomy and the original basal-eutherian test, while later combined matrices can move it outside Theria; topology and scansoriality are not observed ancestry or behaviour.

overview: Nearly complete holotype ROM 55351A preserves elongated wings and a relatively small cochlea used to test the sequence of flight and echolocation specializations.

ecology.diet: Insectivory inferred from dentition; prey not directly preserved
ecology.habitat: Green River lake ecosystem; roosting habitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Powered flight inferred from wing anatomy
ecology.bodySize: Small bat represented by a nearly complete skeleton
ecology.guild: Aerial insectivore inferred, with specialized echolocation unresolved

traits: Claws on all five manual digits
Relatively small cochlea compared with echolocating bats
evidenceSummary: The skeleton supports powered-flight and cochlear-proxy comparisons, but absence of specialized laryngeal echolocation is an inference and the animal is not presented as a direct ancestor.

geography: Lower bone bed, phosphate bed IIa
overview: Holotype skull MNHN PM69 and fourteen referred specimens from Sidi Chennane test primitive proboscidean dental and cranial anatomy in a source-bounded morphology matrix.

ecology.diet: Feeding ecology not directly observed; dental comparisons are bounded functional inference
ecology.habitat: Early Thanetian phosphate-basin setting; habitual habitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Not established by the cranial and dental hypodigm
ecology.bodySize: Estimated 3–8 kg from dental allometry; not directly measured
ecology.guild: No observed guild assigned; broad ungulate-grade comparisons remain interpretive

traits: Fourteen referred upper and lower dental and cranial specimens
evidenceSummary: The hypodigm, locality and skull–tooth anatomy are directly described, whereas stem placement, body mass and ecological interpretation depend on comparative analysis; this fossil is not presented as a direct ancestor.

overview: Holotype right M3 IVPP V20115 and referred teeth and tarsals from the lower Irdin Manha Formation document a Middle Eocene Mimolagus sample used to test mimotonid anatomy and affinity.

ecology.diet: Herbivory inferred from dental morphology; direct food evidence absent
ecology.habitat: Lower Irdin Manha depositional setting; habitual microhabitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Locomotor capability inferred from tarsal comparisons
ecology.bodySize: About 4.5 kg estimated from comparative regressions; not directly weighed
ecology.guild: Large herbivorous duplicidentate inferred from ecomorphology

traits: Holotype right upper third molar IVPP V20115
Dental and tarsal characters scored in mimotonid comparisons
evidenceSummary: Named dental and tarsal material directly records anatomy and the Erlian Basin occurrence; body mass, herbivory, locomotion and lagomorph affinity remain comparative inferences, not an ancestor sequence.
